Excess storage of iron in the body is known as hemosidero-
sis. The high iron stores come from eating excessive iron sup-
plements or from receiving frequent blood transfusions, not 
from increased iron intake in the diet. See Chapter 32.
To reduce the iron from dietary sources, review the list of 
foods and exclude or severely limit their intake until the 
iron overload is alleviated. Pay particular attention to sports 
drinks, energy bars, fortified cereals, and multivitamin min-
eral supplements that have significant amounts of added 
iron.
